target.title: fix(mattermost): strip internal tool-trace banners from outbound text
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mattermost replies can include internal assistant tool-trace failure banners such as `⚠️ 🛠️ ... (agent) failed` when the agent output contains delivery-internal scaffolding. Other text-channel outbound adapters already strip this scaffolding via `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` before delivery, but the Mattermost outbound adapter had no `sanitizeText` hook, so the internal banner could be posted to a Mattermost channel as ordinary user-visible text.

Part of #90684 (apply `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText()` on non-Discord outbound text).

AI-assisted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mattermost outbound adapter now applies the existing `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` delivery sanitizer through the standard `ChannelOutboundAdapter.sanitizeText` hook, matching the established outbound delivery boundary already used by sibling text channels such as Slack, Telegram, Google Chat, IRC, and SMS. The change is a one-line hook plus a focused test; it does not alter Mattermost transport, targeting, chunking, presentation buttons, or config semantics.

## User Impact

Mattermost users receive the intended assistant reply text instead of internal tool-trace diagnostics. Ordinary Markdown prose and outbound chunking behavior are preserved.

## Evidence

Before (on `upstream/main`) the Mattermost outbound adapter exposes no sanitizer, so tool-trace scaffolding would pass straight through to delivery. With the hook reverted to `upstream/main`, the focused test fails because `mattermostPlugin.outbound.sanitizeText` is `undefined`:

```text
$ git stash push extensions/mattermost/src/channel.ts
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts
 FAIL  extensions/mattermost/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts > strips internal tool-trace banners before outbound delivery
AssertionError: expected undefined to be 'Done.' // Object.is equality
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed (2)
```

After this change, driving the real plugin adapter strips the internal banner while preserving ordinary prose:

```text
$ node --import tsx --no-warnings - <<'NODE'
import { mattermostPlugin } from "./extensions/mattermost/src/channel.ts";
const text = "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed";
console.log(JSON.stringify(mattermostPlugin.outbound?.sanitizeText?.({ text, payload: { text } })));
const prose = "The pipeline has 3 open deals.";
console.log(JSON.stringify(mattermostPlugin.outbound?.sanitizeText?.({ text: prose, payload: { text: prose } })));
NODE
"Done."
"The pipeline has 3 open deals."
```

Focused test:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

Type check and formatting:

```text
$ pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
$ pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/mattermost/src/channel.ts extensions/mattermost/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.
$ git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD
```

No live Mattermost round-trip was run because this bug is in the pre-send outbound text-sanitization layer, before any network delivery. The focused test and the direct adapter import verify the exact text produced by the outbound `sanitizeText` seam. Live Mattermost credentials were not available in my checkout, but they are not needed to prove this boundary since the scaffolding is stripped before transport.
